terms.plainEnglish: Shows what changed and what Git is ready to commit.
terms.confusion: It only reports information. It does not change files.

terms.plainEnglish: Stages changed files in the current folder for the next commit.
terms.confusion: It can stage more than you intended, so check git status first.

terms.plainEnglish: Saves staged changes into Git history with a short message.
terms.confusion: It only commits staged changes, not every edited file automatically.

terms.plainEnglish: Uploads your local commits to the connected remote repository.
terms.confusion: Push sends commits, not unsaved file changes.

terms.plainEnglish: Downloads remote commits and applies them to your current branch.
terms.confusion: Pulling with local edits can create conflicts.

commands.whatItDoes: Shows which files have changed and what Git is ready to save.

parts.explanation: Asks Git for the current state of your working folder.

commands.whenToUse: Use this before committing so you know what changed.
commands.commonMistake: Beginners sometimes think status changes files. It only reports information.

commands.whatItDoes: Stages all changed files in the current folder so they can be included in the next commit.

parts.explanation: Means the current folder and everything inside it.

commands.whenToUse: Use this when you want the next commit to include all current changes.
commands.commonMistake: Running git add . can stage more files than you intended. Check git status first.

commands.whatItDoes: Saves the staged changes into Git history with a short message.

parts.explanation: Creates a saved snapshot from the staged changes.
Lets you write the commit message directly in the command.
A short note explaining what changed.

commands.whenToUse: Use this after git add when you are ready to save a meaningful checkpoint.
commands.commonMistake: If nothing is staged, Git will not create the commit. Run git status to check.

commands.whatItDoes: Uploads your local commits to the connected remote repository.

parts.explanation: Sends your commits from your computer to the remote.

commands.whenToUse: Use this after committing when you want your work available on GitHub or another remote.
commands.commonMistake: Push only uploads commits. Unsaved or unstaged file changes will not be pushed.

commands.whatItDoes: Downloads new commits from the remote repository and applies them to your current branch.

parts.explanation: Gets remote changes and merges them into your branch.

commands.whenToUse: Use this when you want to bring your local branch up to date.
commands.commonMistake: Pulling with uncommitted local changes can cause conflicts. Check git status first.

commands.whatItDoes: Creates a new branch and switches you to it.

parts.explanation: Switches which branch you are working on.
Creates a new branch before switching to it.
The name you choose for the new branch.

commands.whenToUse: Use this before starting new work so your changes stay separate from the main branch.
commands.commonMistake: The branch name should not include spaces. Use hyphens, like add-login-page.
